entry.title: UKAEA Senior Visiting Fellow
entry.content: Some exciting news, I have recently become part of the Visiting Academic Scheme with the UK Atomic Energy Authority (UKAEA) as a Senior Visiting Fellow. This allows for much greater collaboration between UKAEA to share our joint expertise and expand any future joint research opportunities. After working with UKAEA for a number of years already (including a co-funded student), I am really excited to continue to build this relationship and contribute to the fantastic work they are doing in the fusion energy area.

entry.title: IReNA Online Seminar
entry.content:
I recently gave a talk for the IReNA Online Seminar series
(https://www.cenamweb.org/events/online-seminar-series) about mirror symmetry and boron-9.

It is really great to get a chance to present recent work by students in my research group to a broad audience where rather than focusing on the nitty-grity of the science - you get to practise presenting a scientific idea in a more basic way, really challenging yourself to make sure the work you are doing is actually interesting!

entry.title: Completion of PGCHE
entry.content: Over the past 14 months I have been completing the University of Birmingham Postgraduate Certificate in Higher Education course. This requires learning about a multitude of different pedagogical areas of higher education covering topics such as how to develop effective teaching and learning, developing skills alongside academic excellence, quality assurance & enhancement, and gaining an understanding of the broader UK Higher Education Landscape. I recently finished the last of three assessed pieces of work and upon completion, am now recognised as a Fellow of AdvanceHE (previously known as Higher Education Academy), the professional body for University Lecturers. It has been a lot of work alongside a full teaching and research load so I am pleased to have finished this requirement at last!

entry.title: Automatic Outreach Materials with AI
entry.content:
The use of AI in many areas of science is taking off, but how about using using LLM to quickly generate outreach materials by giving it a recent paper published and getting a few minute overview at a suitable level for public dissemination?

I tried this last week with a recent paper by my student: A. D. Brooks et al. Phys. Rev. C 111, 024002 (2025) and passing it into the Google NotebookLM where after ten minutes or so you can generate a video overview of whatever content you upload. See the results below:

While it is not perfect and is no substitution for a human-generated effort, it does a pretty good job at highlighting the key important factors of the paper and may generate some useful examples of how to explain this to non-specialists. The future is bright…

entry.title: Neutrons are blue - a manifesto
entry.content:
A manifesto:

Neutrons are blue

Protons are red

Electrons are yellow

Gamma photons are green

Deuterons are orange

Alpha particles are purple
